title: What Is the Fuzz on Old Bread? Explained Simply | PUC Biology Class 11
description:
Diya forgets a loaf of bread in the kitchen for a week, and fuzzy spots spread over it. That fuzz is a living fungus, feeding on her bread. White spots on mustard leaves and a mushroom after the rain belong to the same kingdom: Fungi.

A zoom ladder goes from the bread to one mould spot, the mycelium and one hypha, labelled: chitin wall, coenocytic and septate hyphae. You will see what makes a fungus (heterotrophic, hyphae, saprophytes, parasites, lichens and mycorrhiza), then the four classes run one by one with live animations: Phycomycetes (sporangium, zygospore; Mucor, Rhizopus, Albugo), Ascomycetes (conidia outside, ascospores inside an ascus; Penicillium, yeast, Neurospora), Basidiomycetes (four basidiospores on a basidium; Agaricus, Ustilago, Puccinia) and Deuteromycetes (only conidia; Alternaria, Colletotrichum, Trichoderma). Then ascus vs basidium, a pause-and-think check, a worked sort of six fungi, the imperfect fungi exam trap, an original NEET pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

This is Episode 15 of our PUC Biology series.
Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11 and NEET students.
